extracted.intended_audience: national governments, patent judges, patent litigators, and patent practitioners in EU Contracting Member States
extracted.subtask_description: The Agreement establishing the Unified Patent Court (UPC) setting out its scope, competence, institutional structure, procedural rules, judges' qualifications, and substantive effects of European patents (including unitary patents and supplementary protection certificates) within Contracting Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of the Unified Patent Court
rubrics_metrics.description: A Unified Patent Court for the settlement of disputes relating to European patents and European patents with unitary effect is hereby established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court shall be a court common to the Contracting Member States and thus subject to the same obligations under Union law as any national court of the Contracting Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key definitions (European patent / unitary effect / Statute / Rules of Procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions for terms used in the Agreement, including: 'European patent' (patent granted under the EPC not benefiting from unitary effect), 'European patent with unitary effect' (patent granted under the EPC which benefits from unitary effect under Regulation (EU) No 1257/2012), 'Statute' (Statute of the Court as set out in Annex I), and 'Rules of Procedure' (Rules of Procedure of the Court).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine the scope and application of provisions throughout the Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of application
rubrics_metrics.description: This Agreement shall apply to any: (a) European patent with unitary effect; (b) supplementary protection certificate issued for a product protected by a patent; (c) European patent which has not yet lapsed at the date of entry into force or was granted after that date; and (d) European patent application which is pending at the date of entry into force or filed after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope is subject to Article 83 and other transitional provisions referenced in the Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status and personality of the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall have legal personality in each Contracting Member State and enjoy the most extensive legal capacity accorded to legal persons under the national law of that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court shall be represented by the President of the Court of Appeal elected in accordance with the Statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of the Court (contractual and non-contractual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractual liability of the Court is governed by the law applicable to the contract (Rome I) or failing that by the law of the Member State of the court seized; non-contractual liability for damage caused by the Court or its staff is governed by the law of the Contracting Member State where the damage occurred (Rome II), without prejudice to Article 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court with jurisdiction to settle non-contractual liability disputes shall be a court of the Contracting Member State in which the damage occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court institutional structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall comprise a Court of First Instance (with central, local and regional divisions), a Court of Appeal and a Registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court shall perform the functions assigned by the Agreement and further details (seats, sections) are specified (central division seat in Paris with sections in London and Munich).

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting up local and regional divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Local divisions shall be set up in a Contracting Member State upon its request; an additional local division shall be set up for every 100 patent cases per calendar year commenced in that State during three successive years; a regional division may be set up for two or more Contracting Member States upon their request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of local divisions in a Contracting Member State shall not exceed four. Seats of divisions to be designated by hosting Contracting Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of panels of the Court of First Instance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any panel shall have a multinational composition and, generally, sit in a composition of three judges (with specified variations for local/regional/central divisions including mixtures of legally and technically qualified judges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions set minimum/alternative compositions (e.g., single legally qualified judge in low-volume local divisions; central division usually two legally qualified judges from different Contracting Member States plus one technically qualified judge). Parties may agree to a single judge. Panels are chaired by a legally qualified judge; parties may request allocation of an additional technically qualified judge from the Pool of Judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Court of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any panel of the Court of Appeal shall sit in a multinational composition of five judges: three legally qualified judges who are nationals of different Contracting Member States and two technically qualified judges with qualifications and experience in the field of technology concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels dealing with certain actions (Article 32(1)(i)) may sit with different legally qualified compositions; the Court of Appeal may assign technically qualified judges from the Pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for appointment of judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges shall ensure the highest standards of competence and have proven experience in patent litigation. Legally qualified judges shall possess qualifications required for appointment to judicial offices in a Contracting Member State. Technically qualified judges shall have a university degree and proven expertise in a field of technology and proven knowledge of civil law and procedure relevant in patent litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Advisory Committee delivers proposals on suitable candidates; appointment details set out in the Statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool of Judges and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Pool of Judges shall be established composed of legally and technically qualified judges (full-time or part-time). The Pool must include at least one technically qualified judge per field of technology; judges may be allocated to divisions based on legal/technical expertise, linguistic skills and relevant experience to guarantee uniform high quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation mechanisms and list content are governed by the Statute and Rules; Registry maintains list indicating linguistic skills, field of technology, experience and cases previously handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training framework for judges
rubrics_metrics.description: A training framework, with facilities in Budapest, shall be set up to improve patent litigation expertise and ensure broad geographic distribution of knowledge. It shall focus on internships in national patent courts, improvement of linguistic skills, technical aspects of patent law, dissemination of civil procedure knowledge for technically qualified judges, preparation of candidate-judges, and provide continuous training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular meetings shall be organised between judges to discuss developments and ensure consistency of case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy and application of Union law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall apply Union law in its entirety and shall respect its primacy. Decisions of the Court of Justice of the European Union shall be binding on the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court shall cooperate with the CJEU and request preliminary rulings in accordance with Article 267 TFEU to ensure uniform interpretation of Union law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of Contracting Member States for infringements of Union law by the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Member States are jointly and severally liable for damage resulting from an infringement of Union law by the Court of Appeal; action for damages may be brought against the Contracting Member State where the claimant has residence or place of business, or where the Court of Appeal has its seat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules on contribution among Member States and procedural detail to be determined by the Administrative Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of law to be applied by the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: When hearing cases, the Court shall base its decisions on: (a) Union law (including Regulations (EU) No 1257/2012 and 1260/2012); (b) this Agreement; (c) the EPC; (d) other international agreements applicable to patents and binding on all Contracting Member States; and (e) national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Court bases decisions on national law, applicable law is determined by directly applicable Union private international law, international instruments on private international law, or failing those, national private international law provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to prevent direct use of the invention (patent proprietor's exclusive rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent confers on its proprietor the right to prevent any third party not having the proprietor's consent from: (a) making, offering, placing on the market or using a product which is the subject-matter of the patent, or importing or storing the product for those purposes; (b) using a process which is the subject-matter of the patent or offering the process for use where the third party knows or should have known consent is required; (c) offering, placing on the market, using, or importing or storing for those purposes a product obtained directly by a process which is the subject-matter of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets out direct infringement acts actionable before the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to prevent indirect use of the invention (supplying essential means)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent confers the right to prevent third parties from supplying or offering to supply, within the territory where the patent has effect, any person (other than a party entitled to exploit the invention) with means relating to an essential element of that invention for putting it into effect, when the third party knows or should have known those means are suitable and intended for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 2 excludes staple commercial products except where the third party induces the person supplied to perform acts prohibited by Article 25; Paragraph 3 excludes certain entitled persons from being considered non-entitled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and exceptions to patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights conferred by a patent shall not extend to acts done: (a) privately and for non-commercial purposes; (b) for experimental purposes relating to the subject-matter of the patented invention; (c) use of biological material for breeding or discovering other plant varieties; (d)-(l) specified statutory exceptions (e.g., pharmacy extemporaneous preparation, use on board foreign vessels temporarily entering waters, acts allowed under certain EU directives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific sectoral and situational exceptions; these limit scope of enforceable rights before the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right based on prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who would have had, if a national patent had been granted, a right based on prior use of that invention or a right of personal possession shall enjoy the same rights in respect of a patent for the same invention in that Contracting Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes prior-user defence/rights against later patent proprietors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights conferred by a European patent shall not extend to acts concerning a product covered by that patent after that product has been placed on the market in the European Union by, or with the consent of, the patent proprietor, unless there are legitimate grounds for the patent proprietor to oppose further commercialisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out exhaustion doctrine (regional/EU exhaustion) for goods placed on the market in the EU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of supplementary protection certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplementary protection certificate shall confer the same rights as conferred by the patent and shall be subject to the same limitations and the same obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPCs are treated as extending the patent's effects subject to same limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International jurisdiction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The international jurisdiction of the Court shall be established in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 or, where applicable, on the basis of the Lugano Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines cross-border jurisdictional basis for UPC cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive competence of the Court
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall have exclusive competence in respect of: (a) actions for actual or threatened infringements of patents and SPCs and related defences; (b) declarations of non-infringement; (c) provisional and protective measures and injunctions; (d) revocation of patents and declaration of invalidity of SPCs; (e) counterclaims for revocation/invalidity; (f) actions for damages or compensation derived from provisional protection conferred by a published European patent application; (g) actions relating to use of the invention prior to granting or right based on prior use; (h) actions for compensation for licences on the basis of Article 8 of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2012; and (i) actions concerning decisions of the EPO in carrying out tasks under Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 1257/2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National courts remain competent for matters not falling within the Court's exclusive competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence of divisions of the Court of First Instance (allocation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions for infringement, provisional measures, damages linked to provisional protection, and actions relating to prior use shall be brought before: (a) the local division where the infringement has occurred or may occur (or regional division); or (b) the local division where the defendant has residence or place of business (or regional division). Certain actions must be brought before the central division (declarations of non-infringement and revocation). Special rules apply for defendants outside Contracting Member States, consolidation, first-seized division competence, and referral of revocation counterclaims to the central division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets forum/venue rules, prohibits multiple proceedings between same parties on same patent across divisions, and provides discretions for panels regarding counterclaims and referrals between divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registry duties and public register
rubrics_metrics.description: A Registry shall be set up at the seat of the Court of Appeal and sub-registries at all divisions. Subject to conditions, the register kept by the Registry shall be public. The Registry shall keep records of all cases, notify cases upon filing, publish decisions (subject to confidentiality), publish lists of notifications and withdrawals of opt-outs, and publish annual reports with statistical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registrar is responsible for organisation of the Registry and ensuring opt-out information is notified to the European Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making, secrecy and dissent
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberations of the Court shall remain secret. Decisions of panels are taken by majority (presiding judge's vote prevails on equal votes in even-number panels); decisions contain names of judges and are signed; dissenting opinions must be reasoned, given in writing and signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules specify quorums for full court decisions and signature/reading in open court for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision by default procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision by default may be given where a party, after being served with proceedings, fails to file written submissions or appear at oral hearing; an objection may be lodged within one month of notification of the default decision. Objection does not automatically stay enforcement unless the Court decides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism and time-limits for default judgments and their contestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) and stay of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures established by the CJEU for referrals for preliminary rulings apply. Whenever the Court of First Instance or Court of Appeal decides to refer a question of Union law interpretation/validity to the CJEU, it shall stay its proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures uniform interpretation of EU law and binding effect of CJEU rulings on the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of technical subject-matter within the central division
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases within the central division are distributed among sections (London section, Paris seat, Munich section) according to the International Patent Classification into 8 sections (A to H) (e.g., Chemistry, Physics, Electricity, Mechanical engineering, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation to Paris/London/Munich sections follows the IPC classification to align technical expertise with case distribution.
